summary: Derives "which files move together" by walking git log --name-status -M and counting files that change in the same commit; stores 8 partners per file, shows 3, min support 2, 12k-commit window (all measured, don't retune blind). The non-obvious part is canonicalizeRenames: -M labels ONLY the rename commit, so every older commit still records the old path and a renamed file silently splits into two half-histories whose older half is keyed to a path that no longer exists and can never be displayed. Because git log is newest-first, the fix is a single forward pass carrying an alias map — a rename old->new seen at commit i means every LATER entry in the stream (i.e. older commit) that says old means new — resolved transitively and only ever recorded backwards, so a path later reused by a different file keeps its own identity. Verified 2026-08-23 on arches: 12k commits in 596ms, 325KB sidecar.

The non-obvious part is canonicalizeRenames: -M labels ONLY the rename commit, so every older commit still records the old path and a renamed file silently splits into two half-histories whose older half is keyed to a path that no longer exists and can never be displayed. Because git log is newest-first, the fix is a single forward pass carrying an alias map — a rename old->new seen at commit i means every LATER entry in the stream (i.e. older commit) that says old means new — resolved transitively and only ever recorded backwards, so a path later reused by a different file keeps its own identity. Verified 2026-08-23 on arches: 12k commits in 596ms, 325KB sidecar. 2026-08-25, for consumers computing a RATIO: `touched` is NOT a count for every file in history — it is trimmed to `keep`, i.e. files that got a partner list plus those partners, so a file whose every pair fell below min-support has NO entry at all and any shared/touched calculation must read that absence as silence rather than a zero denominator. Every file that HAS partners does have its denominator, so a ratio gate needs no extra data.
